value.title: Introduction to Backpropagation
value.summary: This chapter introduces backpropagation as the core algorithm enabling neural networks to learn. It outlines the video's goal: providing an intuitive walkthrough of backpropagation without relying on complex formulas, setting the stage for a deeper mathematical exploration in the next video.

value.title: Prerequisites and Problem Setup
value.summary: The video establishes foundational knowledge required to understand backpropagation, including neural network structure, forward propagation, gradient descent, and the concept of minimizing a cost function. It focuses on the classic task of recognizing handwritten digits using the MNIST dataset.

value.title: Cost Function and Gradient Descent
value.summary: This section explains how the cost function is calculated by summing squared differences between predicted and actual outputs across training examples. It emphasizes that learning involves finding the negative gradient of this cost function to efficiently reduce error through weight and bias adjustments.

value.title: Intuitive Understanding of Gradients
value.summary: The chapter breaks down the gradient vector as a set of sensitivities, showing how each weight and bias affects the cost function. It uses a concrete example to illustrate that some weights have a much larger impact on cost than others, guiding efficient learning.

value.title: Backward Propagation of Changes
value.summary: This segment explains how to determine the desired changes to weights and biases by working backward from the output layer. It describes how each neuron's desired activation change influences the previous layer, forming the basis of backpropagation.

value.title: Single Example Adjustment
value.summary: The video focuses on how one training example (a handwritten '2') influences weight and bias adjustments. It details how to nudge output neurons toward their target values and how those changes propagate backward through the network.

value.title: Recursive Backpropagation
value.summary: This chapter explains the recursive nature of backpropagation, where the desired changes to one layer are used to compute changes for the previous layer. It emphasizes that all output neurons' desires are combined proportionally to their weights and required changes.

value.title: Averaging Over All Examples and Mini-Batches
value.summary: The video covers how to aggregate adjustments from all training examples to compute a true gradient. It introduces stochastic gradient descent using mini-batches for computational efficiency, explaining the trade-off between accuracy and speed.

value.title: Conclusion and Practical Considerations
value.summary: The chapter summarizes backpropagation as an algorithm for determining optimal weight and bias changes per example. It concludes with practical insights about data requirements, the importance of labeled datasets like MNIST, and the role of computational efficiency in real-world training.
